title: API 570 Training in Toledo, OH: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 570 exam prep for Toledo piping inspectors: hydroprocessing, coker and asphalt piping, CUI, injection points, dead legs and blanks, self-paced online.
h1: API 570 training in Toledo: exam preparation for process piping inspectors at the Oregon and Lima refineries and the pipeline terminals around them
html:
API 570 exam prep for process piping inspectors around Toledo

On any refinery near Toledo the piping outnumbers the vessels many times over. It runs from crude manifolds to hydrocracker reactors, along racks carrying hot asphalt, sour water, hydrogen and caustic side by side, out to tank farms and pipeline connections. Every circuit needs CMLs, a corrosion rate, a class and an interval. The API 570 Piping Inspector certification is the credential owner-users and contractors ask for when they hand that job to one person.

Atlantis NDT's API 570 course is preparation for API's examination, studied online and self-paced. You start when you enrol, choose your own pace and send questions to an instructor, who answers from the text of API 570, B31.3 or whichever document applies. There is no Atlantis classroom in Toledo, and the company's offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. The American Petroleum Institute sets eligibility, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification.

Piping systems behind the Toledo-area unit lists

EIA's 2026 Refinery Capacity Report shows why piping work differs between the plants in reach of Toledo. Each unit brings circuits with their own damage, and an inspector's first job on a new site is to learn which circuits those are.

  • PBF Energy's Toledo refinery appears in EIA's listing with an 82,000 barrel-per-stream-day catalytic cracker, a 52,000 barrel distillate hydrocracker, a high-pressure reformer and a gasoline desulfurization unit, and PBF names an alkylation unit and a UDEX aromatics unit among its major units and xylene, toluene, nonene and tetramer among its petrochemicals. That means catalyst-laden lines prone to erosion, high-pressure hydrogen and reactor effluent piping, acid-service piping in the alkylation unit and solvent circuits in aromatics extraction.
  • Cenovus's refinery in Oregon, Ohio runs a 72,500 barrel vacuum unit, a 36,000 barrel delayed coker, a gas oil hydrocracker and 9,000 barrels per stream day of asphalt capacity. Hot heavy-oil and residue lines, coker blowdown and sour water piping, and long runs of heat-traced asphalt line come with that list.
  • Cenovus's Lima refinery, in Allen County, combines coking, hydrocracking, high-pressure reforming and an aromatics plant, so a Lima piping inspector meets most of both patterns on one site.
  • Marathon's Detroit refinery, to the north, is a coking refinery with 32,000 barrels per stream day of asphalt capacity, which means plenty of traced and insulated heavy-product piping.

The damage mechanisms on the 2027 API 570 list, matched to Toledo circuits

The Body of Knowledge API published for its 2027 API 570 windows names fifteen RP 571 paragraphs, plus the definitions in Section 2, and limits RP 571 questions to those. The table pairs each with a circuit a Toledo-area inspector is likely to meet.

RP 571 paragraphMechanismWhere to picture it around Toledo
3.3Amine stress corrosion crackingRich and lean amine lines around contactors and regenerators, especially unrelieved carbon steel welds
3.8 and 3.22Atmospheric corrosion; corrosion under insulationRacks exposed to lake-effect weather, insulated and traced lines, supports that trap water
3.9Boiler water and steam condensate corrosionCondensate return and tracing supply headers
3.14 and 3.15Caustic corrosion; caustic stress corrosion crackingCaustic injection lines and treaters, and steam-traced caustic piping
3.17Chloride stress corrosion crackingAustenitic stainless lines under wet insulation or near cooling water
3.27Erosion and erosion-corrosionCatalyst and slurry lines on catalytic crackers, coker lines carrying fines, elbows after control valves
3.31Galvanic corrosionDissimilar-metal joints at alloy upgrades and repairs
3.37Hydrochloric acid corrosionCrude unit overhead piping, and reformer effluent where chlorides come off the catalyst
3.43Mechanical and vibration-induced fatigueSmall-bore connections near pumps, compressors and control valves
3.45Microbiologically influenced corrosionFire water, cooling water and other low-flow water systems
3.57Soil corrosionBuried road crossings, tank farm lines and soil-to-air interfaces
3.58Sour water corrosion (acidic)Overhead and sour water piping on cokers, crackers and hydroprocessing units
3.61SulfidationHot crude, vacuum and coker transfer lines, most pronounced at the higher-sulfur plants

Several mechanisms Toledo piping inspectors deal with every year are not on that list: wet H2S damage, high-temperature hydrogen attack, naphthenic acid corrosion, sulfuric acid corrosion and ammonium salt corrosion in hydroprocessing effluent. Some of them appear on API 510's list instead. Learn them for the job, not for this exam, unless your window's Body of Knowledge adds them back.

Corrosion under insulation on traced and asphalt lines through a Lake Erie winter

Corrosion under insulation grows quietly on every site in this climate: water gets under cladding at damaged jacketing, unsealed penetrations, support clips and low points, and snow and ice keep feeding it. RP 571 and API 570 describe the operating temperature ranges in which carbon steel and austenitic stainless steel are most susceptible; learn those bands from the editions on your effectivity sheet rather than from a summary, because exam options are written to test exactly where the edges sit. Lines that cycle in and out of those ranges, and lines that sit idle, are worse than lines that run steadily hot.

Two Toledo-area features push CUI up the list. Asphalt and heavy-oil lines are steam- or electrically traced and fully insulated, and a leaking steam tracer keeps the insulation wet from the inside. Older racks also carry lines whose service has changed several times, so a line now running cool may have been insulated for a hot service it no longer has. API 570 asks owners to plan CUI inspection for susceptible systems and gives a suggested extent of examination by piping class; read that guidance in your edition rather than memorising percentages from a study guide. For methods and their limits, see the CUI detection guide.

Injection points and mix points on hydroprocessing and crude units

Injection points concentrate damage into short lengths of pipe, which is why API 570 treats them as circuits of their own. Around Toledo the common ones are wash water injected upstream of hydroprocessing reactor effluent coolers to keep ammonium salts in solution, neutralising and filming chemicals added to crude unit overheads, caustic injected into crude charge, and inhibitors dosed into sour or overhead streams. Each one changes the chemistry of the pipe downstream, sometimes for the better and sometimes, when the injection nozzle fails or the dose is wrong, sharply for the worse.

For the exam, know three things. API 570 defines how far upstream and downstream of the injection point the circuit extends, and that definition is a favourite closed-book question. Injection point circuits carry a shorter maximum thickness interval in API 570's Table 1 than Class 1, 2 or 3 circuits do. And RP 574 explains where to place CMLs and which examinations suit the area, including where radiography or ultrasonic scanning finds what spot readings miss. Mix points, where hot and cold or wet and dry streams join, behave in a similar way and deserve the same scrutiny in a CML plan.

Dead legs, idled branches and a worked example on permanent blanks

Both Cenovus plants in Ohio have operated for more than a century, and refineries with a long history of revamps tend to carry dead legs left over from projects long finished: a bypass that is never opened, a branch to a pump that was removed, a drain stub that sees water and nothing else. In Toledo winters, dead legs in water or wet service can also freeze. API 570 expects dead legs to be identified and inspected, and a branch truly out of service is often better removed or isolated with a permanent blank, which makes the B31.3 blank calculation more practical than it looks.

A permanent blank is to be fitted between Class 150 raised-face flanges on a line designed for 275 psig. The problem gives a gasket inside diameter of 8.75 in., an allowable stress of 20,000 psi for the plate, a quality factor E of 1.0, a weld joint strength reduction factor W of 1.0 and a corrosion allowance of 0.0625 in.

  1. B31.3 paragraph 304.5.3: t = dg × √(3P ÷ 16SEW) + c.
  2. 3P ÷ 16SEW = 825 ÷ 320,000 = 0.002578, and its square root is 0.0508.
  3. Pressure thickness = 8.75 × 0.0508 = 0.444 in.; add the corrosion allowance to get 0.507 in.

A half-inch plate is therefore just too thin, and the next standard plate up is needed. Exam options are built around that slip and two others: leaving out the corrosion allowance (0.444 in.) and using the wrong diameter. For raised-face and flat-face flanges the code uses the gasket inside diameter, while for ring joint and fully retained gaskets it uses the gasket pitch diameter, so read which flange type the question describes before you calculate.

Where API 570 stops at Toledo's pipeline connections

Crude and products move in and out of the Toledo refineries mainly by pipeline, and the plant boundary is where an API 570 inspector's scope usually ends. Mid Valley Pipeline Company's tariff effective July 2026, published through Energy Transfer, lists crude delivery points at Toledo and at Lima, alongside Samaria in Monroe County, Michigan, with origins reaching back to Longview, Texas. Sunoco LP's Toledo products terminal takes receipts from Sunoco Pipeline and Buckeye Pipeline, and Buckeye's 2024 directory of connecting facilities lists connections at Toledo for Cenovus, PBF, Marathon and others, together with a Buckeye-owned West Toledo terminal.

Cross-country pipelines are regulated by PHMSA under 49 CFR Part 195 and are built and maintained to their own codes; plant and terminal piping on the owner's side of the boundary is where API 570 programmes normally apply. The owner's documents define where one regime ends and the next begins. For the code's own scope rules, see the API 570 standard overview.

Getting to API 570 eligibility from a Toledo job

API counts education plus piping experience gained within the last ten years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency, which includes an owner-user inspection organisation. One year of supervising or performing inspection is enough with a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology; a two-year degree or certificate needs two years in all, one of them in inspection; a high school diploma needs three; and no formal education needs five or more. Detail is on the API 570 certification requirements page.

  • UT thickness technicians on refinery and terminal contracts collect the readings API 570 programmes run on. Learning to evaluate them, set corrosion rates and propose intervals is what turns that work into inspection experience. In the United States Atlantis performs UT, MT, PT and VT and does not perform radiography; see ultrasonic testing in Toledo.
  • Pipe welders. Owens Community College's pipe welding certificate prepares students for ASME Section IX testing, and repair and fabrication years count towards the longer routes. The inspection year has to come from inspection work.
  • Operators moving into a unit inspection role already know where each line goes and what it carries.
  • Engineers from the University of Toledo or elsewhere reach eligibility fastest with a bachelor's degree, once they have a year in inspection.

Working B31.3 and API 570 into a Toledo rotation

The open-book half of API 570 largely tests how fast you can find things in B31.3 and B16.5, a skill built over several rotations rather than in one push.

  1. API 570 and RP 574 first. Learn the class definitions, the corrosion rate and remaining life formulas and the interval table well enough to work closed-book.
  2. B31.3, by the Body of Knowledge list. Pressure design thickness under 304.1.2, quality factors from 302.3 and Table A-1B, blanks under 304.5.3, impact test exemption from Figure 323.2.2A, preheat and heat treatment in section 330, leak tests in 345 and expansion in Appendix C.
  3. B16.5. Find the material group, then the rating table, and practise working out the most economical flange class for a given pressure and temperature.
  4. RP 571's fifteen paragraphs. Use the table above and attach each mechanism to a line you know.
  5. Timed papers on screen. Because the code books are PDFs on the exam computer, practise searching and paging in PDFs rather than flicking through tabbed paper copies.

When a problem will not come out, such as a B31.3 thickness that looks too thin or a B16.5 rating that falls between tables, send it to the instructor with your working; the answer points to the paragraph as well as the number.

Sponsoring a piping inspection group from a Toledo site or contractor

Refinery owner-users and inspection contractors around Toledo often prepare several people together, for example a UT crew moving into inspection roles, or unit inspectors who need API 570 before a contract renewal. Send one enquiry with the number of candidates and the windows they are aiming at, and fees are quoted on request. Each candidate studies individually, applies to API individually and must meet the experience rules personally, so check their records before enrolling them.

faq.q: Is there an API 570 classroom course I can attend in Toledo?
faq.a: Atlantis does not run one: there is no Atlantis classroom in Toledo, and the API 570 course is self-paced online study with an instructor who answers your questions. Some other providers run fixed-date seminars, in person in other cities or online. Whatever you choose, the API 570 examination itself is sat in person at a Prometric test centre.

faq.q: Is wet H2S damage on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Not in the Body of Knowledge for the 2027 API 570 windows. Its RP 571 list covers fifteen paragraphs, among them sour water corrosion, hydrochloric acid corrosion, sulfidation, amine cracking and corrosion under insulation, but not wet H2S damage, which appears on the API 510 list instead. Check the Body of Knowledge for your own window, because API revises it.

faq.q: Do fire water lines at a Toledo refinery fall under API 570?
faq.a: API 570 treats water services, fire protection systems included, as piping an owner may choose to include in or leave out of the inspection programme, so it depends on the site. Microbiologically influenced corrosion, the mechanism that most often attacks those systems, is on the current RP 571 list, so learn it either way.

faq.q: Is the permanent blank calculation really on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Yes. The Body of Knowledge lists the minimum required thickness of a permanent blank under B31.3 paragraph 304.5.3. Watch three details: add the corrosion allowance, use the gasket inside diameter for raised-face flanges but the pitch diameter for ring joints, and do not round the result down to a thinner standard plate.

faq.q: I take thickness readings at the Oregon refineries for a contractor. How close am I to API 570?
faq.a: Taking readings builds piping experience; evaluating them, setting rates and recommending intervals is the inspection part API looks for. With a high school diploma you need three years of piping experience including one in inspection, gained while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency. Keep a log of circuits and tasks for your application.

faq.q: Are the pipeline delivery lines at a Toledo terminal covered by API 570?
faq.a: Usually not. Transportation pipelines are regulated by PHMSA under 49 CFR Part 195, and the owner's documents set the boundary between pipeline and plant or terminal piping. Transfer and process piping inside the terminal or refinery fence is where an API 570 programme normally applies.

faq.q: Should a Toledo piping inspector take API 570 or API 510 first?
faq.a: Take the one your experience record supports. Contract UT technicians and rack inspectors usually have more piping than vessel experience, so API 570 comes first, and unit inspectors often add API 510 later. The exams share Section V, Section IX, RP 571, RP 577 and PCC-2 material, so the second is easier.

faq.q: Can a Toledo contractor enrol its whole UT crew for API 570 prep?
faq.a: Yes. A single quote can cover every technician you put forward. They each follow the course on their own timetable, put their piping questions to the instructor, and later make an individual application to API. Confirm beforehand that each technician's documented experience satisfies API's rules.
